concepts.def: Pressure when goals seem out of reach

walkthroughs.body_html:
Crime has many causes:

  • Inequality — poverty pushes some to crime.
  • Peer pressure — friends in gangs.
  • Poor schooling.
  • Family breakdown.
  • Addiction.

Sociologist Robert Merton said: when society sets big goals (money, fame) but blocks the legal path, some choose crime to reach them.

That's strain theory.

Ways to prevent crime:

  • Good schools and youth clubs.
  • Jobs and apprenticeships.
  • Mental health support.
  • Tackling poverty.

Prison is the end — prevention is cheaper. 💷

mcqs.q: Why do positivists and interpretivists prefer different methods?
options: Positivists treat sociology like natural science, seeking objective measurable patterns — preferring quantitative methods. Interpretivists believe humans construct meaning, requiring qualitative methods to access subjective experience.
Positivists like numbers and interpretivists like words — that's the whole difference.
It is a recent invention of capitalism.
Both positivists and interpretivists prefer experiments above all else.

mcqs.q: What is a self-fulfilling prophecy in education?
options: A self-fulfilling prophecy is when teachers predict the future accurately.
A self-fulfilling prophecy is when a student predicts their own grade correctly.
It is a recent invention of capitalism.

When teachers' expectations (often based on labels) influence pupil behaviour and achievement — pupils labelled as 'bright' tend to do better, those labelled 'thick' worse, regardless of underlying ability (Rosenthal and Jacobson).

options: It is a recent invention of capitalism.
It is universal and performs four essential functions in all societies.
It is the only valid family form and others are dysfunctional.
